messages:
dina: paging: GPU OOMs on live-decode pool starting ~03:14 UTC, several streaming requests dropped. incident bot fired. I'm paged. Anyone oncall for runtime?
inc-bot: INCIDENT CREATED #INC-20250314-73 (sev2) — GPU OOMs causing streaming request drops. Pager: dina. Response window: 15m.
opsbot: Node alerts: node-gpu-08 flapping, container restarts x3 in last 10m. GPU memory metric spiked to 98%.
ashwin: oncall-ashwin here, looking. can you drop the trace id for a dropped request?
dina: trace: 9a4f3b2c, sample logs show decode loop continuing past user max_tokens. suspect runaway generation. pasted logs below:
```
2025-03-14T03:13:52Z [worker-7] request_id=9a4f3b2c model=redwood-2-large streaming=true user_max_tokens=256 generated=2048
2025-03-14T03:13:53Z [worker-7] CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 1.2G
2025-03-14T03:13:54Z [worker-7] killing request, dropping connection, metrics: token_rate=400 t/s
```
lee: that first line shows `generated=2048` while `user_max_tokens=256` — likely a bug in streaming decode stop condition or prompt containing an instruction to keep going.
marta: any recent deploys to runtime?
deploy-bot: Deploy 2025-03-14T02:58:11 UTC: runtime-service v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4 (canary).
ashwin: v1.12.4 introduced a change to streaming termination where we use `stop_on_max_tokens` flag default true, but there is an edge-case when `streaming=true` + nonzero `max_tokens` + client-sent stop tokens: it can fail to decrement remaining tokens. grabbing commit now.
ashwin: quick mitigation: disable streaming on the model route for all incoming requests for now (config toggle). That will force non-streaming generation with stricter post-checks. Who can flip the route?
sam: i can do the toggle via console. will put a global route override and add a circuit-breaker for `decode` endpoints. applying now.
sam: done — disabled streaming for route: /v1/generate/redwood-2-large (override id: ov-20250314-1). added header `X-Force-Streaming: false` for internal requests.
opsbot: routing change propagated to 10/12 runtime nodes, waiting for remaining nodes.
dina: good. can we also lower default `max_tokens` guard to 512 for the next 30m? need to reduce memory spikes.
lee: I'll patch the runtime config. changing default_user_max_tokens: 2048 -> 512 and enabling strict enforcement in the decode loop. applying to canary nodes first.
lee: patch applied to canary nodes (node-gpu-11, node-gpu-12). Monitoring memory metrics.
opsbot: node-gpu-08 still flapping (restarts). kube logs show OOMKill in container runtime-server. Here's snippet:
```
Mar 14 03:15:10 node-gpu-08 kubelet[...]: Container runtime-server terminated with signal 9 (OOMKilled)
Mar 14 03:15:10 node-gpu-08 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4211 (runtime-server) score 987
```
ashwin: suspect the worker already in runaway state and then OOM kills container; need to drain node-gpu-08 and cordon. I'll start a drain.
marta: I can open the customer impact tracking doc and update.
sam: cordoned node-gpu-08 and started eviction. traffic shift in progress.
opsbot: traffic to node-gpu-08 reduced to 0; pending pod evictions 5.
dina: customer impact: real-time streaming customers saw dropped connections. early estimate: ~120 dropped requests across 3 customers in the past 12m. two customers reported elevated errors via support @support.
marta: adding to incident doc: impacted customers = [Acme Analytics (prod), Nimbly Chat (staging), AtlasDocs (prod)]. severity reported: Acme saw user-facing errors, Nimbly minor retries.
ashwin: long-term fix: add an enforced token budget check in the decode inner loop, and a safety cap that aborts if generated_tokens > user_max_tokens * 3 (in case of client override). Also add mem-check before allocating large buffers. Raising PR now.
ashwin: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/482 (draft) — includes: strict decrement of remaining_tokens, guard against negative remaining, early abort path with error code `ERR_MAX_TOKENS_EXCEEDED`.
ashwin: propose backfill hotfix to v1.12.4 -> v1.12.4-hotfix1 with the guard only, then rollout to all nodes.
sam: agree. I'll coordinate a quick rolling restart canary -> full. can we get a +1 from runtime on the risk?
lee: hotfix is small and low-risk, but we should keep streaming disabled until we confirm it's safe. I'll +1 the hotfix.
marta: communication: drafting a short note for support and account teams with timeline and mitigations. will post a status update in #customer-updates.
dina: handoff: my shift ends in ~20m. ashwin, can you take over the oncall and keep streaming disabled until hotfix is rolled and metrics look stable for 30m? log what you change.
ashwin: taking over oncall. I'll monitor GPU memory, dropped request count, and confirm rollout.
ashwin: immediate next steps for new oncall: 1) approve hotfix release, 2) canary rollout to 2 nodes, 3) monitor memory + errors for 30m, 4) full rollout if stable, 5) re-enable streaming on routes and observe.
opsbot: metric snapshot: peak GPU mem = 98.6% (03:14:53), dropped_stream_conns = 123 (last 15m), container_restarts = 4 (last 20m).
marta: customer comm plan: 1) tell affected customers we mitigated immediate issue (streaming disabled) and are working on hotfix; 2) offer to replay/ingest any lost inputs for Acme if they want; 3) will follow up with RCA after postmortem.
sam: starting hotfix release pipeline: tagging v1.12.4-hotfix1, building image.
sam: hotfix image built and pushed: gcr.redwood/runtime:v1.12.4-hotfix1. triggering canary deploy now.
deploy-bot: Rolling update started: v1.12.4-hotfix1 -> nodes: node-gpu-11,node-gpu-12 (canary).
opsbot: canary status: node-gpu-11 healthy, node-gpu-12 healthy. memory profiles show no spikes in the last 4m.
ashwin: good. proceed to rolling update across remaining nodes in batches of 2.
sam: rolling update in progress. currently 6/12 nodes updated.
nina: (note: nina isn't in participants list, please ignore)
opsbot: rolling update complete: 12/12 nodes on v1.12.4-hotfix1.
opsbot: post-rollout metrics: peak GPU mem = 65%, dropped_stream_conns = 2 (last 30m).
dina: great — hotfix looks effective. request to re-enable streaming on /v1/generate/redwood-2-large in 15m if metrics stay stable.
ashwin: agreed. I'll keep streaming disabled for 30m post-rollout, then re-enable on canary routes first.
marta: documenting handoff: oncall -> ashwin at 03:34 UTC. incident status: mitigation in place, hotfix rolled, customer comm drafted. next: postmortem and follow-up actions.
ashwin: tracking follow-ups: 1) full postmortem (owner: marta), 2) add unit+integration tests for streaming stop conditions (owner: lee), 3) add e2e test with malicious prompts that try to force extra tokens (owner: ashwin), 4) add runtime metric alert for generated_tokens > user_max_tokens * 2 (owner: ops).
marta: ETA for postmortem draft: EOD today. will schedule RFC for alert thresholds next week.
dina: handing off. thanks team. :pray:
ashwin: taking over — will update this thread with any new customer reports or if we re-enable streaming.
opsbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, hotfix rolled, impact limited to 3 customers, incident moving to monitoring state.
